metaDescription: Assess cloud identities, permissions, configurations, storage, network controls, logging and data protection with Cybersentinels cloud security services.

blocks.text: Strengthen Security Across Your Cloud Environment
Cybersentinels Consulting assesses cloud environments for identity, configuration or network

sections.heading: Cloud Risk Often Begins with Configuration and Identity

blocks.text: Cloud platforms provide powerful security capabilities, but they also introduce complex identities and permissions
Depending on platform and scope, assessment may include:
Identity and Access Management
Review users, roles and service identities
Network Security
Assess virtual networks, routing and security groups
Storage and Data Protection
Review public access, permissions and encryption
Logging and Monitoring
Evaluate security logging, audit trails and alerting
Compute and Workload Configuration
Assess security-relevant configuration of virtual machines, containers, serverless services or managed workloads in scope
Security Posture and Misconfiguration
Identify high-risk configuration weaknesses and gaps against relevant provider and organizational practices
Secrets and Keys
Review observable handling of credentials, tokens, keys and secrets across relevant services
Resilience and Recovery
Evaluate selected backup, recovery and availability controls where included
Governance and Account Structure
Review ownership, account organization and guardrails
1. Architecture and Scope Review
Understand providers, accounts and subscriptions
2. Access and Evidence Planning
Agree on read-only access, exported configuration, documentation and security-tool evidence required for the assessment
3. Configuration and Control Assessment
Review identities, permissions and network controls
4. Exposure and Attack-Path Analysis
Identify public exposure, excessive privileges and combinations of weaknesses that may increase impact
5. Risk Prioritization
Consider exploitability, data sensitivity and workload criticality
6. Reporting and Roadmap
Provide prioritized findings, corrective recommendations and a practical improvement roadmap
7. Validation Support
Review remediation evidence or reassess selected configurations where included
Useful scoping information includes:

items: Number of accounts, subscriptions or projects
Available read-only access or exported configuration

sections.heading: When to Conduct a Cloud Security Assessment

items: After rapid cloud expansion or architectural change
When consolidating multiple accounts or subscriptions
Before a compliance assessment or customer review
After a cloud-related incident or exposure
When introducing containers, serverless or new managed services
As part of recurring cloud-governance and posture management
Assessment aligned with cloud architecture and shared responsibility
Focus on identity, configuration and exposure
Risk prioritization based on workload and data context
Coverage across governance and technical controls
Ability to map findings to compliance requirements where relevant

blocks.text: Cloud assessment coverage depends on the providers, accounts and services
Do you require administrative access?
Not necessarily
Can you assess multiple cloud providers?
Yes, subject to agreed scope and service coverage
Is a cloud assessment the same as cloud penetration testing?
No
Can findings be mapped to a compliance framework?
Where relevant and agreed, findings can be associated with applicable control areas
